name: Vants
miniText: Can a deterministic rule appear irregular while remaining reversible? NetLogo Vants moves virtual ants across a binary patch field, toggling the visited color and turning right or left according to that color. Langton [1] provides the artificial-life context, Gale and colleagues [2] investigate generalized ant dynamics, and Turing [3] supplies the broader connection between local read-write rules and computation. The original NetLogo rule moves before examining and changing the new patch, so operation order is part of its identity. Its world wraps, and multiple ants share the same writable field. Initial headings, ant count, activation order, and finite boundaries affect the visible trace. The model illustrates how simple deterministic interactions can generate long transients and structured paths; apparent disorder is not evidence of stochasticity, and reversibility requires an explicitly defined inverse update.
